title: Individualized Entropic-Risk Allocation with Publicly Calibrated Catastrophe Probabilities
banked_reason: D-0.5 REJECT at letter tier: exact-public-calibration benchmark is below field and reaching field requires changing the central information regime; independent validity gate confirms stop under operator below-floor policy.
gap_reasons: The policy-regret headline omits the closer published policy-learning literature, notably ParnasEtAl2026 on conditional preference/distributional treatment effects and policy-value maximization; the remaining exact-known-atom specialization is a narrow technical benchmark and ranks below the required field floor.

Its consumer, “The allocation consumer receives an explicit evaluable sample-size and calibration benchmark,” names neither a paper, applied domain, nor open problem, so it does not establish a field-facing implication.

Exact, externally known equality of the ceiling-atom probability across every covariate value and both potential-outcome arms is load-bearing, while the stated hypothetical external-catastrophe story supplies no realistic domain or validation path for that exact calibration.
proof_attempt_summary: The supervisor-authorized exact-topic retry produced angle 0 v2, correcting the endpoint-policy sign and separating arbitrary real data access from finite-precision computation. D-0.5 rejected the proposal at letter tier because exact public common-atom calibration has no credible validation path or field-facing consumer; independent boundary and terminal validity reviews found no same-coordinate field salvage. No D0 derivation, Lean module, or formal theorem was completed; unknown or misspecified atom calibration is a different experiment for a future topic.
tldr: Publicly calibrated equal catastrophe probabilities remove atom-mass uncertainty from individualized entropic-risk allocation. For the full unknown-body and unknown-propensity observational class, expected integrated excess conditional loss risk has matched order \(\epsilon^{3/2}\min\{(n\epsilon)^{-\beta/(2\beta+1)},n^{-\beta\lambda/(2\beta\lambda+\lambda+2\beta)}\}\), with exact zero regret at saturation. Direct Laplace learning and endpoint extrapolation attain the two branches; exact normalized body alternatives give a converse for every randomized original-record policy. A tagged finite encoding supports a certified executable attainer. Attainment from ordinary real-number names without catastrophe tags is an explicit open question.
gap: Regular conditional distributional treatment-effect theory and direct-arm EVaR identification do not give a matched conditional allocation frontier uniform in a shrinking known common atom deficit.
fill: The exact-risk localization, two learning channels, and normalized complete-record testing embedding deliver the full policy-regret transition. Explicit numerical access and error contracts connect the statistical upper to an executable encoded-data rule.
